title: the same four alias spellings over a callback that cannot throw need no contract: the program compiles and each spelling really invokes the callback
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': the obligation to spell `Result<A, E>` attaches to a value that CAN fail. A total callback cannot, so no spelling of a reference to it may require a contract. This is the over-correction guard for `an-aliased-fallible-callback-still-needs-a-contract`: that case requires the callback-boundary resolver to start following a `const` binding, a second `const` binding and an object property to the function they hold, and the cheap way to satisfy it is to refuse a callback argument that is not a literal function expression. This file is what that costs, and the direction is not hypothetical — this repository has shipped seven over-corrections, and the resolver widening that closed the alias hole is exactly the kind of change that produces one. EACH LINE PASSES A DIFFERENT KEY, so the four printed values are `ADA`, `BOB`, `CYD` and `DEE` rather than four copies of one string. That is deliberate: it means the case observes that each spelling reached the consumer AND that the consumer invoked the callback with that spelling's own argument, so a lowering that collapsed, reordered or duplicated the four calls produces something visibly wrong instead of a permutation of identical lines. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: a total callback aliased through a mutable binding, which is a recorded open residual on both backends for the fallible direction and therefore cannot be paired honestly here. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the third declared stdout line from `CYD` to `BOB` — making the double-alias row print the single-alias row's value, which is what a resolver that collapsed the two hops onto one binding would produce — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 fe811d30ec743a2b01b9335830890da97443c4f7db9e2d54634fb8a4fbd5777f before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
